dialogue.chat: A conversation, free of charge? Consider it an investment in us, %1$s. Proceed.
dialogue.chat/1: Free consultation? For you, %1$s, I'll waive the fee. This once. Proceed.
dialogue.chat/2: A chat costs me working time, you know. Consider it a gift. I don't give many. Go on.
dialogue.conversations: Talk? Fine — first consultation's free, %1$s. After that we discuss rates.
dialogue.conversations/1: Talk's cheap, they say — and I do love a bargain. Go on, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations/2: You've my ear. The rest of me is still working, mind. Time's money.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.good: Excellent week. Eggs are up, expenses are down, and the baker owes me two favors. The portfolio thrives.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.good/1: In the black this week. Profits up, losses down, and a favor owed to me. Couldn't ask for better numbers.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.good/2: Thriving, thank you. Even the weather's been thrifty — free sunshine all week.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.rough: Terrible margin this week — six days in, one decent soup out. Your asking, though... I'll book that as income.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.rough/1: Poor returns lately. But you asking after me? I'll enter that as unexpected income, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.again: Asked already, %1$s. I don't discount the same answer twice — that's just giving product away.
dialogue.conversations.checkin.again/1: Twice now? You're generous with the concern. I'll note the surplus and still say: fine.
dialogue.conversations.day.good: Profitable. Found a nail, sold nothing at a loss, and the well water's still free. They'll fix that oversight someday.
dialogue.conversations.day.good/1: Turned a tidy profit doing nothing expensive. Best kind of day — the cheap kind.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough: A net loss of a day. Dropped an egg — that's one whole egg — and lent the miller my ladder. I'll see neither again.
dialogue.conversations.day.rough/1: Down an egg and a ladder. Small sums, but they add up, and I feel every copper of it.
dialogue.conversations.work.like: I love it. Every blister converts to bread eventually. Show me another investment with returns like that.
dialogue.conversations.work.like/1: Love it — sweat converts straight to coin, given time. Name me a safer investment.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate: The hours are theft and the pay is worse. I've done the math — I stay out of stubbornness, which at least costs nothing.
dialogue.conversations.work.hate/1: The pay's an insult, but quitting costs more than staying. I stay out of pure economics, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.village.home: %2$s? Decent market, reliable foot traffic, low rent on account of the smell by the tannery. Sound investment, home.
dialogue.conversations.village.home/1: I know every debt and favor owed in %2$s, %1$s. That's not gossip — that's bookkeeping.
dialogue.conversations.people.first: Good customers, most of them. A few slow payers. I keep a ledger of who owes whom — it's practically a map of the village.
dialogue.conversations.people.first/1: Reliable folk, if you count the coin after. I like them fine. I like them better when they settle up, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.food.first: Whatever's cheapest per bite and fills the longest. I didn't get this pantry by paying inn prices.
dialogue.conversations.food.first/1: Free is my favorite flavor. The well water, a neighbor's guilt-gift, that sort of thing. Tastes like savings.
dialogue.conversations.life.first: The whole story? Premium inventory, %1$s. But you pay attention, and that's the rarest coin. Fine — chapter one, free of charge.
dialogue.conversations.life.first/1: My story's premium stock — but you listen, and attention's the rarest currency. First chapter's on the house.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.first: A pantry so full I could lend flour at NO interest, just to see their faces. Don't you dare tell anyone I said that.
dialogue.conversations.dreams.first/1: A vault so full I could give some away just to watch their faces. ...You heard nothing.
dialogue.conversations.fears.first: Honestly? Dying with full pockets and an empty table. What was I saving it all FOR, then? ...Forget the second part.
dialogue.conversations.fears.first/1: A full purse and an empty table at the end. What's the hoard FOR, then? ...Strike that.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.first: I ran the numbers, %1$s. Time with you: costly. Returns: unreasonable. You're the one thing I'd overpay for. Don't quote me.
dialogue.conversations.feelings.first/1: You're the one expense I never resent, %1$s. Terrible for the books. Wonderful otherwise. Don't tell the ledger.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.personal: That information isn't for sale yet — and I sell almost everything. Build some credit with me first. You're good for it, I think.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.personal/: That's not on the market yet, and I'll sell nearly anything. Build credit with me first.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.intimate: Ha — that one's in the locked chest under the locked chest. Keep investing, %1$s. You're the rare account I hope matures.
dialogue.conversations.deflect.intimate/: Locked chest, under a locked chest. Keep investing, %1$s — you're the account I actually hope pays out.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.none: Nothing worth trading. A quiet week — bad for gossip, worse for business. Even the chickens are withholding.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.none/1: No news worth trading. Bad week for gossip, worse for business. Even the hens are holding out on me.
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.yes: Happy? You're the one line item I never regret, %1$s. Priceless — and I've priced everything. Yes.
dialogue.conversations.us.happy.yes/1: I'd trade the whole vault for you and call it a bargain. Don't let that get out — it'd ruin my reputation.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.marriage: %2$s and %3$s got hitched. Two incomes, one roof — shrewd, actually. And the feast? I catered half of it at a healthy markup.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.marriage/1: %2$s married %3$s. A merger, if you ask me. Combined pantries, shared debts. I'll adjust both their ledgers accordingly, %1$s.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.divorce: %2$s and %3$s split. Do you know what dividing a household costs? Two of everything now. Grim for them — but the market for spare furniture just improved.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.divorce/1: So %2$s and %3$s are through. Assets to divide, debts to reassign... messy business. I've already offered my services. For a modest fee.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.death: %2$s passed on. A shame — genuinely. They also owed me for a sack of grain, and one doesn't press an estate too soon. I'll wait. Respectfully.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.death/1: We lost %2$s. Good soul, always paid on time — that's the highest praise I've got, and I mean it, %1$s. The village is poorer for it, in every sense.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.birth: %2$s was born! A new mouth to feed, yes, but also a future customer. I'm playing the long game — I'll have their loyalty before they can hold a coin.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.birth/1: There's a baby, %2$s. Wonderful — and do you know what swaddling cloth fetches right now? I'm not made of stone, %1$s. Congratulations to them, truly.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.arrival: %2$s moved in. New customer, fresh purse, no idea what things cost around here yet. I mean — welcome, welcome. Lovely for the village.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.arrival/1: Someone named %2$s settled here. More foot traffic past my stall, and I do like a growing market. Nice for the community too, obviously.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.departure: %2$s moved away for good. There goes a paying customer — and worse, they never settled that last tab. I'll be feeling that loss for a while.
dialogue.conversations.gossip.departure/: %2$s packed up and left. One less account on my books. The village shrinks, the market shrinks... it all costs something, %1$s.
